Ollama Embeddings API for Local Document Search

Send an array of page texts to Ollama’s POST /api/embed and read one vector per input from embeddings. Embed the question with the same model, then rank the page vectors by cosine similarity. Open the highest-ranked source and verify that it contains the answer. When a scanned page is missing from the input, add its OCR text before rebuilding the index.

  1. Get an embedding batch
  2. Run the Python example
  3. Find the failing step
  4. Check ranking and vector dimensions
  5. Check for missing source text
  6. See the measured results

Get an embedding batch from Ollama

Start Ollama on your computer and install an embedding model. The example uses nomic-embed-text:v1.5. Check the installed tag with ollama list.

ollama pull nomic-embed-text:v1.5

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"nomic-embed-text:v1.5","input":["search_document: The Extended tier retains records for 45 days.","search_query: How long is Extended retention?"],"truncate":false}'

Look for two arrays under embeddings, in input order. The example uses Nomic’s document and query prefixes. For another model, check its own instruction format. The older /api/embeddings example uses prompt and returns embedding. Use the matching fields for the endpoint you call.

If the request fails, check ollama list, use the exact tag, and confirm the server port. Choose an embedding-capable model. With truncate: false, an input that exceeds the model’s window fails instead of silently losing its end.

Rank the sample pages from Python

Download the ranking script and the three-page sample text into the same folder. With Ollama running, use Python 3.10 or later. The script uses the standard library and calls only the loopback embedding endpoint.

python3 rank-support-pages.py

For a different local port, add --port and the port number. Our local trial imported the publisher’s F16 GGUF after a registry download failed. To reproduce that exact import, save the GGUF beside a Modelfile with the following line, then create the sample tag from that folder:

FROM ./nomic-embed-text-v1.5.f16.gguf
ollama create ipunk-nomic-embed:v1.5 -f Modelfile
python3 rank-support-pages.py --model ipunk-nomic-embed:v1.5

The script embeds three pages and three questions together. It prints the vector dimensions and two rankings for each question, with and without the OCR page. Pass --vectors to include all input strings and returned vectors.

Check dimensions and ranking inputs

  • Count the returned vectors and compare their dimensions before ranking. This test returned six vectors of 768 coordinates.
  • Use the same embedding model and dimensions for the question and every document. Rebuild the document index when you switch embedding models, even if the new vectors have the same length.
  • Check the model’s query and document prefixes. Inspect the actual top-ranked text and retain its page number. A high similarity score gives you a candidate to read.

Check that the answer exists in your source text

Search your extracted text for the expected phrase or ID before tuning ranking. The first two pages of our sample PDF contained selectable text. Page 3 was an image, so the original Markdown had no escalation rule. The MarkItDown conversion and OCR guide shows how the missing text was recovered.

Include the corrected text as its own page or chunk, keep a source reference and rerun the same question. A scan that contains an important table or identifier warrants checking the OCR against the page.

What changed when page 3 entered the index

Top-ranked page for each exact test question
QuestionMarkdown onlyWith OCR page
SCAN-43 deadlinePage 2, no answerPage 3, 72 hours
Extended retentionPage 2, 45 daysPage 2, 45 days
BASIC-52 reviewPage 1, supervisor reviewPage 1, supervisor review

For SCAN-43, page 2 scored 0.604 before and after OCR was added. Page 3 scored 0.845 once it was a candidate, and it contained the deadline. Only the candidate set changed between rankings. The test used one synthetic document, three questions and Ollama 0.40.18 on macOS with external networking blocked during inference. It measures retrieval on this fixture. No language model generated an answer.
